name: M5 (mtDNA)
description: Mitochondrial haplogroup M5 is a South Asian branch of M found at notable frequencies among scheduled castes and Romani (Roma) populations. In India, M5 is found primarily among Dalit and lower-caste communities at frequencies of 3–8%, suggesting an ancient South Asian origin before the establishment of the caste system. Crucially, M5 was identified as one of the founding mtDNA haplogroups of the Romani people of Europe — a population originating from a single migration out of northwestern India approximately 1,000–1,500 years ago. The presence of M5 in European Romani at frequencies of 10–30% directly links the Romani diaspora to their South Asian ancestry.
interestingFact: Haplogroup M5 served as a key genetic 'smoking gun' that confirmed the South Asian origins of the Romani people. When geneticists found M5 — a haplogroup rare outside India — at high frequencies among Roma communities across Europe, it provided definitive proof that the Romani people originated from a single migration from northwestern India roughly 1,000 years ago.
